title: Sector-specific CII categorization overlay for the sphere of science

act.effective_date_note: The act states no special commencement rule; 2026-03-15 is derived from first official publication on 2026-03-07 and the general seven-day rule.

governance_rules.rule: Defines sector-specific categorization and calculation of significance indicators for CII objects in the sphere of science.

Covered science-sector CII subjects are state bodies and state institutions that lawfully own or operate relevant information systems, telecommunication networks or industrial control systems, plus state bodies and state institutions that provide interaction of those systems or networks.
Categorization must account for sector specifics and current statutory lists of typical sector CII objects.
Categorization uses article 7 of Federal Law 187-FZ, PP 127 base rules and indicator thresholds, and this overlay together.
Computer incident and computer attack retain the meanings defined by Federal Law 187-FZ.
Identify systems matching typical sector objects, assess possible incident consequences under the significance indicators, then assign a category or decide that no category is necessary.
When a CII object is modernized, the subject may decide to divide it into several separate CII objects.

An object outside the current typical-object lists is not excluded when possible incident consequences meet significance criteria and values: assign the most suitable category and send object information plus proposals to amend the lists to the federal CII-security authority. The submitted information follows PP 127 clause 17.

Assess targeted-attack worst cases and maximum possible harm without silently crediting existing controls, analogue-process duplication or paper fallback; account for process and object dependencies, threat feasibility and prior incident statistics.

Categorization is based on possible attacks and incidents in the stated R&D context at technology-readiness level not lower than seven, including scientific or scientific-technical results at that level, and depends on the clause 9 indicators.

calculation_rules.rule: Determine applicability of significance criteria to the information system, telecommunication network or industrial control system before calculating indicator values.
If significance indicators are inapplicable to the object, their values are not calculated.
Determine possible incident consequence scale from identified information-security threats, attack types, object purpose and automated-process purpose.
Assess possible incident consequences under only the indicators routed by clause 9.
Count incidents that may negatively affect an object on whose operation R&D under an international treaty of the Russian Federation depends.
Count possible reduction in subject tax payments or other budget contributions when an object participating in R&D malfunctions.
Count possible emissions, discharges or spills of harmful and polluting substances into air, water bodies or soil from object malfunction during R&D.
For state-defence-order R&D, count possible reduction in output over a specified period and possible increase in unit-production time as percentages of the specified output or established unit time.

guardrails: Do not expand clause 2 from state bodies and state institutions to every scientific organization.
Do not omit Federal Law 187-FZ, PP 127 or current typical-sector-object lists.
Clause 7 permits an object split after modernization but does not require it.
An object outside the current typical-object lists is not automatically out of scope when its possible consequences meet significance criteria and values.
Do not invent an overlay-specific submission, review or reporting deadline: PP 246 contains no numerical time obligation.
The minimum value seven in clause 11 is a technology-readiness threshold, not a category number, deadline or evidence-retention period.
Do not silently credit existing controls, analogue duplication or paper fallback in the clause 10 maximum-harm scenario.
Applicability must be decided before calculation; inapplicable indicators are not calculated.
Positions 1, 7, 9, 11 and 13^1 must not be interchanged; each has a distinct triggering context and consequence logic.
No category is proven until complete facts and the applicable PP 127 threshold comparison are documented.
